prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the other person roughly 1–2 m in front of the camera wearer, with the metal pipes mainly to his left and slightly behind/beside him, while the walls and stairs lie farther away at roughly 3–5+ m; the lower edge is nearest to the wearer. Across frames 1–2 he remains at a similar distance, in frame 3 the wearer’s hand and the held metal fittings enter the near foreground within about 0.2–0.6 m and partly occlude him, frame 4 clears again, and frame 5 repeats this close foreground occlusion. It makes foreground–background separation and arm’s-reach regions clearer than RGB, including that some pipe ends near the person are within his reach while most of the laid-out pipes are farther left. Exact metric distances are uncertain because the map is monocular, and several pipes, body boundaries, stairs, and the near hand/fittings merge into smooth or saturated depth regions.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map consistently isolates one person about 1–2 m ahead, positioned near the center of each frame, but it identifies almost none of the many pipes, tools, walls, or stairs visible in RGB. Small masks labelled “carrot” in frame 1 and “wine glass” in frame 5 appear spatially inconsistent with the RGB objects and are likely classification errors, while a bottom-edge region labelled “person” in frame 5 is probably the camera wearer’s partly visible hand or arm. The person’s mask shifts slightly right-to-left with the viewpoint and becomes elongated downward in frame 3 where the foreground arm/objects overlap him, revealing occlusion but not dependable object identity or separation. This map makes the person’s silhouette and occupied image region clearer than RGB, but it is unreliable for scene layout, inter-object distances, facing direction, and the numerous thin overlapping metal objects it fails to segment.
descriptions.pose: The pose map places the other person’s upper body near the center, with the head above the torso and both arms extending forward/down toward objects that are within roughly an arm’s length of him. His torso and head orientation indicate that he generally faces the camera wearer and appears directed toward the camera in frames 1–4, then turns or angles somewhat to his left in frame 5 while remaining about 1–2 m away. The skeleton shifts lower and slightly left in frame 3 as the viewpoint and foreground occlusion change, then returns higher in frame 4; hand keypoints show changing arm configurations even where hands are difficult to distinguish in RGB. The map clarifies joint layout, body orientation, and reach, but several hand points float or fragment, legs are largely absent because the person is crouched and occluded, and no reliable pose is recovered for the camera wearer’s partly visible foreground arm.
